payload.acceptance_criteria:
WHEN a README quickstart command runs in a repository of the other storage kind, THE KIT SHALL refuse by name and print the form for that kind.
WHEN sync names the frozen ledger in a vault repository, THE KIT SHALL name `sync` or `sync --vault`, not a mirror.
A test runs every README command in a ledger repository and in a vault repository.
payload.description:
## Context

Reproduced 2026-11-26 19:19-19:20 UTC by basicly-tracker-kit. In a local-ledger repository, README forms `claim RECORD-ID`, `comment RECORD-ID --text ...` and `sync` exit 2 with argparse 'the following arguments are required: record' or 'directory', because the id is read as the directory. In a vault repository, `sync .basicly/ledger` refuses with 'start a mirror with `basicly-tracker init --mirror beads`', a remedy for another feature; bare `ready`, `list` and `create` exit 2 for a missing directory while bare `claim`, `comment` and `sync` work. Customer impact: the first commands a customer copies fail with parser noise or a wrong remedy.
payload.title: Make the README quickstart CLI forms work, or refuse by name, in both ledger and vault repositories

payload.acceptance_criteria:
WHEN status runs in a repository set up by init --scope project or by vault-init, THE KIT SHALL exit 0 and name the storage, the pinned version and the tool version.
--help SHALL describe the init scopes as the README does.
A test runs status after each documented setup.
payload.description:
## Context

Reproduced 2026-11-26 19:19 UTC by basicly-tracker-kit. After `basicly-tracker init --scope project`, and in a vault repository, `basicly-tracker status` exits 1 with 'tracker: not installed at .basicly/kit/tracker'. The frozen ledger guard notice tells the customer to 'use basicly-tracker status'. `--help` says init vendors the kit into ./.basicly/kit/tracker, while the README says plain init installs for the user. Customer impact: a correctly installed repository reports itself as not installed.
payload.title: Make status report the installed tracker instead of a vendored kit path

payload.acceptance_criteria:
Every vault subcommand usage line SHALL start with the program name that ran it.
The package README links SHALL resolve from the published package page.
A test checks both.
payload.description:
## Context

Seen 2026-11-26 19:20 UTC by basicly-tracker-kit. `basicly-tracker vault-init --help` and the vault claim usage error print 'usage: cli.py ...'. The package README links ../../.basicly/core/kit/tracker/REFERENCE.md and SPEC.md, which resolve only inside this repository tree, not in an installed or published package. Customer impact: low; confusing help and dead links outside GitHub.
payload.title: Print the basicly-tracker program name in vault command usage and fix package README links

payload.text:
Standalone kit audit, 2026-11-26 19:24 UTC, package 0.3.0 at main 9a1314f3 (measured in scratch installs). Ranked by customer risk:
1. basicly-bi81emt.1: vault-init preview prints a next command without --prefix; running it publishes genesis, exits 0, attaches nothing; retry refused "already has commits". Customer is stuck.
2. basicly-bi81emt.2: no supported way to attach a second repository to an existing vault, though the README sells multi-repository vaults. Needs a design decision.
3. basicly-bi81emt.3: held-by claim refusal prints next "claim ID --take --reason ... --vault URL"; the parser refuses --take and --reason.
4. basicly-bi81emt.4: version-pin refusal names "basicly-tracker update", which refuses; --version prints 0.3.0 for v0.49.5 and main; README install unpinned, no upgrade section; uv tool upgrade says nothing to upgrade.
5. basicly-bi81emt.5: README quickstart forms (claim ID, comment ID, sync) fail with parser errors in a ledger repository; "sync .basicly/ledger" in a vault names a beads mirror remedy.
6. basicly-bi81emt.6: status says "not installed" after every documented setup; the frozen guard tells customers to run it.
7. basicly-bi81emt.7: usage lines say cli.py; README links break outside the repository.
Known and held by basicly-tracker: jw1kmii (fsck .basicly/ledger traceback in a vault, reproduced again).
Passed: claim race of two sessions and two machine identities gave one winner; 6 parallel comments from 2 sessions all reached the vault; vault-check valid.
Not checked: Windows and macOS, CI consumer job for the git+https install.

payload.acceptance_criteria:
A test collects every command the kit prints as a remedy or next step: refusals, previews, status and the package README quickstart.
The test runs each collected command in a scratch local ledger and in a scratch vault.
The test fails on an argparse error, an unknown verb or a traceback, and names the printed command and the place that printed it.
payload.description:
## Context

Orchestrator order 2026-11-26 19:25 UTC on the kit audit (comment on basicly-bi81emt.1). basicly-bi81emt.3, .4, .5 and .6, the earlier "share --vault" remedy and the "fsck .basicly/ledger" form in a vault are one class: the kit prints a next command that does not work. Fixing each one alone does not stop the next. When the kit prints a remedy or next step, I want a test to run it, so a customer never meets a command with a parser error or a missing verb. Ranked right after basicly-bi81emt.1; .3 to .6 become its first red cases.
payload.title: Contract test: run every command the kit prints as a remedy or next step

payload.text: Scope change on basicly-bi81emt.1: vault-init --yes without --prefix stays allowed where tests pin it (outside a checkout, and before migrate --to-vault of an existing ledger). The fix: (a) the preview next keeps --prefix; (b) in a Git checkout with no .basicly/ledger and no .basicly-tracker.toml, --yes without --prefix refuses before it pushes and names the --prefix form. Checked 19:26 UTC: no existing command attaches a new repository to a genesis-only vault (migrate refuses "source holds no events"), so that way out belongs to basicly-bi81emt.2. The program name in vault next fields moves to basicly-bi81emt.7.
